item.title: Solvent-solvent dipole engineering of a low-concentration electrolyte for high-performance wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries
item.description:

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers solvent-solvent dipole engineering in low-concentration electrolytes, a strategy not previously applied to sodium-ion batteries. By tuning dipole interactions, it simultaneously overcomes poor low-temperature conductivity and high-temperature interfacial instability, enabling wide-temperature operation while cutting salt use and cost—advancing practical, sustainable sodium-ion battery deployment.

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using chaotropic anions to tune ionic coordination and the dynamic electrode–electrolyte interface, suppressing zinc dendrites and hydrogen evolution. 💡 Zwitterionic additives in water-in-salt electrolytes decouple conductivity from viscosity, shifting them from subionic to superionic Walden behavior. This arises from competitive coordination: zwitterions bind Li⁺ yet weaken Li⁺–TFSI⁻ association, redistributing water. The work reveals a design route to independently tune solvation, ion correlations, and transport in concentrated electrolytes.

item.title: Multi-Step Oxygen Redox Mechanism in the Polyanionic Lithium-Rich Cathode Li2FeSiO4

💡 This study overturns the assumption that polyanionic frameworks prevent O2 formation in lithium-rich cathodes. It reveals FeSiO4 decomposes via a multistep oxygen redox mechanism involving Fe migration, disproportionation, and O2 release, showing previously proposed mechanisms can act as steps in one process. This advances understanding of silicate cathode stability and guides design of durable lithium-rich materials.

💡 The work integrates a stress-adaptive Si-Zn-amorphous carbon anode with a salt-segregated PVDF-HFP electrolyte, creating a polymeric-inorganic bilayer interphase. item.title: Escaping the Polymerization-Kinetics Trap in Ether Electrolytes for Durable Silicon Interphases

💡 The novelty lies in identifying a polymerization-kinetics trap: stronger polymerization in trioxane electrolytes worsens silicon interphase durability by depleting species prematurely. Adding LiNO3 suppresses early trioxane activation while enabling nitrate-derived passivation, yielding a thinner, coherent interphase. This kinetic regulation significantly improves cycling stability, offering a new design principle for durable silicon anodes.
